data.exact_reserve_text: Syndicate 958 has benefitted from positive reserve development relating to prior periods. An improvement in the old years' catastrophe events resulted in reserve releases across the Global Property and Global Specialty business units, which includes favourable developments on Casualty and Motor XL classes on older years of account. In the 2014 calendar year, the 2014, 2013 and 2012 & prior years of account have all contributed profits (2014: GBP 4.0m; 2013: GBP 3.8m: 2012 & prior: GBP 23.5m).

prior_year_events.impact_description: Materially impacted the 2012 year of account and contributed to brought forward losses on the 2012 year of account (part of the GBP 23.1m brought forward losses for 2012), though the year later benefitted from favourable reserve development.
Cited as one of the major losses that materially impacted the 2012 year of account (contributed to brought forward losses), subsequently partially offset by favourable reserve development.

named_events.loss_description: The net ultimate claims from this storm are forecast to be GBP 1.1m.
Materially impacted the 2012 year of account and contributed to brought forward losses on that year.
Cited as a major loss impacting the 2012 year of account.

data.standardized_narrative: Syndicate 958 experienced a net prior-year release in 2014 totalling GBP 27.3m (net profit contributions from 2013 and 2012 & prior years of account), equivalent to approximately a 6.5% release against opening gross claims outstanding. The releases arose from favourable reserve development on older years, driven by improvement in old-years catastrophe events and favourable developments on Casualty and Motor XL classes, while the syndicate had a modest 2014 exposure to Hurricane Odile (forecast net loss GBP 1.1m).

data.data_quality_notes: Prior year development (-27.3m) is derived from the year-of-account profit contributions disclosed (2013: GBP 3.8m; 2012 & prior: GBP 23.5m) and represents net underwriting profit contributions by year of account rather than a directly reported GROSS movement in insurance liabilities. Lob movements are taken from the 'favourable/(adverse) run-off deviation' table (these figures appear to be NET of reinsurance and are presented in the report in GBP 000). No explicit gross ('insurance liabilities') prior-year movement note was provided, so net/year-of-account sources were used. Confidence in numeric lob breakdowns is moderate (0.5) due to net basis and small rounding.
